questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Procurement Management in a project?
questions.option_a: A. To acquire products, services, or resources from external sources while managing cost, quality, risk, and supplier relationships
questions.option_b: B. To define the internal organizational structure of the project team
questions.option_c: C. To calculate the critical path of the project
questions.option_d: D. To estimate the duration of every project activity
questions.explanation: Procurement Management focuses on acquiring products, services, or resources from external sources while managing cost, quality, risk, and supplier relationships.

questions.question: Which procurement process determines what must be obtained externally and how procurement will be managed throughout the project lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Planning Procurement determines external procurement requirements and establishes how those procurements will be managed.

questions.question: Which activity is specifically associated with procurement planning?
questions.explanation: Make-or-buy analysis is performed during procurement planning to determine whether work should be developed internally or purchased from a vendor.

questions.question: An IT project team must decide whether to develop a cloud monitoring component internally or purchase an existing service. Which procurement activity directly addresses this decision?
questions.explanation: Make-or-buy analysis evaluates whether a required product or service should be developed internally or obtained from an external vendor.

questions.question: Which document can be prepared during procurement planning to request detailed proposals from potential vendors?
questions.explanation: A Request for Proposal (RFP) is one of the procurement documents identified for obtaining vendor proposals.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a vendor selection criterion in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies cost, experience, quality, and technical capability as vendor selection factors.

questions.question: Which procurement process involves obtaining seller responses, evaluating suppliers, and awarding contracts?
questions.explanation: Conducting Procurements includes obtaining seller responses, evaluating vendors, negotiating contracts, and selecting sellers.

questions.question: A project manager sends an RFQ to several vendors and receives quotations from them. Which procurement activity is occurring?
questions.explanation: Collecting proposals, quotations, and technical submissions is the receiving seller responses activity.

questions.question: During proposal evaluation, which combination is most appropriate according to the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Cost, quality, experience, technical capability, and delivery schedule
questions.option_b: B. Employee age, office location, and personal preferences
questions.option_d: D. Only the vendor's company size
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies cost, quality, experience, technical capability, and delivery schedules as proposal evaluation factors.

questions.question: A project manager is discussing pricing, timelines, service levels, and legal terms with a potential supplier before signing an agreement. What activity is this?
questions.explanation: Negotiating contracts involves discussing pricing, timelines, service levels, and legal terms before final agreement.

questions.question: Which procurement process focuses on monitoring supplier relationships and ensuring contractual obligations are fulfilled?
questions.explanation: Controlling Procurements monitors seller performance, manages contracts, reviews deliverables, and handles procurement changes and payments.

questions.question: A vendor is consistently delivering software later than the agreed schedule. Which controlling procurement activity is most directly relevant?
questions.explanation: Monitoring seller performance involves tracking whether vendors meet schedule, cost, quality, and service requirements.

questions.question: A supplier submits an invoice that does not match the agreed contract terms. Which controlling procurement activity should address this issue?
questions.explanation: Managing payments and claims includes verifying invoices, approving payments, and addressing disputes or claims.

questions.question: Which action belongs to Closing Procurement rather than Controlling Procurement?
questions.explanation: Archiving contracts, reports, correspondence, and procurement documentation is part of closing procurement.

questions.question: A project has finished all vendor work. Before formally closing the procurement, the manager verifies that all contracted deliverables have been received and accepted. What process is being performed?
questions.explanation: Verifying that all products or services were delivered according to contract requirements is a closing procurement activity.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Resource Management?
questions.option_a: A. It focuses only on purchasing equipment from vendors
questions.option_b: B. It identifies, acquires, develops, manages, and controls project resources
questions.option_c: C. It only calculates project duration
questions.option_d: D. It only manages external suppliers
questions.explanation: Resource Management covers identifying, acquiring, developing, managing, and controlling resources needed to complete the project.

questions.question: Which process establishes how project resources will be estimated, acquired, managed, utilized, and controlled?
questions.explanation: Planning Resource Management defines the overall approach for estimating, acquiring, managing, utilizing, and controlling resources.

questions.question: Which activity is part of Planning Resource Management?
questions.explanation: Planning Resource Management includes identifying resource needs, defining roles and responsibilities, developing team strategies, and planning communication.

questions.question: Which process determines the type and quantity of resources required to complete project activities?
questions.explanation: Estimating Activity Resources determines the types and quantities of resources needed for project activities.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical resource identified in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Servers, laptops, and networking devices are examples of physical resources.

questions.question: A project manager examines each work package and determines that the testing activity needs three testers and two testing environments. Which process is primarily being performed?
questions.explanation: Determining the required types and quantities of people and equipment is part of estimating activity resources.

questions.question: Which process focuses on obtaining team members, equipment, materials, facilities, and other resources needed for project execution?
questions.explanation: Acquiring Resources obtains the human and physical resources required to execute project work.

questions.question: A functional manager assigns a developer to a project based on the developer's skills, experience, and availability. Which resource activity does this represent?
questions.explanation: Assigning team members involves allocating individuals according to skills, experience, and availability.

questions.question: Which process primarily focuses on improving team competencies, skills, collaboration, and overall effectiveness?
questions.explanation: Developing the Team improves competencies, skills, collaboration, and team effectiveness.

questions.question: A project manager introduces technical workshops, mentoring, and team-building activities to improve team capability. Which process is being emphasized?
questions.explanation: Training, mentoring, workshops, and team-building activities are key activities in Developing the Team.

questions.question: Which activity is most directly associated with Managing the Team?
questions.option_a: A. Monitoring team performance and resolving conflicts
questions.option_c: C. Estimating project duration using historical data
questions.explanation: Managing the Team includes monitoring performance, providing feedback, resolving conflicts, motivating members, and facilitating collaboration.

questions.question: Two developers disagree about implementation responsibilities and the disagreement is reducing project productivity. Which Resource Management activity is most directly applicable?
questions.explanation: Resolving conflicts is a key activity of Managing the Team.

questions.question: Several engineers are assigned simultaneously to multiple projects, causing workload conflicts. Which Resource Management process is most directly responsible for addressing this issue?
questions.explanation: Controlling Resources includes managing resource shortages, overlaps, and scheduling conflicts.

questions.question: Which activity is part of Controlling Resources?
questions.explanation: Controlling Resources involves monitoring resource utilization, comparing actual and planned usage, resolving conflicts, optimizing allocation, and maintaining records.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Schedule Management?
questions.option_b: B. To plan, develop, monitor, and control the project timeline
questions.option_c: C. To train all project team members
questions.explanation: Schedule Management ensures project activities are planned, coordinated, monitored, and controlled so that the project is completed on time.

questions.question: Which scheduling technique identifies the longest sequence of dependent activities that determines the minimum project completion time?
questions.explanation: CPM identifies the longest sequence of dependent activities that determines the shortest possible project duration.

questions.question: Which scheduling technique represents activities, durations, timelines, and progress using horizontal bars?
questions.explanation: Gantt charts display activities, durations, timelines, and progress using horizontal bars.

questions.question: A project manager plans near-term work in detail but keeps future activities at a higher level until more information becomes available. Which technique is being used?
questions.explanation: Rolling Wave Planning progressively plans near-term work in detail while keeping future work at a higher level.

questions.question: Which process establishes the policies, procedures, tools, and methodologies for managing the project schedule?
questions.explanation: Planning Schedule Management establishes the approach, procedures, tools, performance methods, and baselines used to manage the schedule.

questions.question: Which process converts work packages into specific tasks that can be scheduled and monitored?
questions.explanation: Defining Activities breaks down work packages into manageable activities and prepares activity lists.

questions.question: A project manager examines the WBS, breaks work packages into detailed tasks, identifies milestones, and creates an activity list. Which process is this?
questions.explanation: These are the key activities listed under Defining Activities.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Sequencing Activities?
questions.option_b: B. To identify and document logical relationships and dependencies among activities
questions.option_c: C. To calculate employee performance ratings
questions.explanation: Sequencing Activities determines the logical order and dependencies among project activities.

questions.question: In a software project, system testing cannot begin until software development has finished. Which dependency is represented?
questions.explanation: Finish-to-Start means the successor cannot start until the predecessor has finished.

questions.question: A database configuration activity can start once application coding has started, even though coding has not yet finished. Which dependency best represents this relationship?
questions.explanation: Start-to-Start means the successor cannot start until the predecessor has started.

questions.question: Documentation updates cannot be completed until system testing has been completed. Which dependency is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Finish-to-Finish means the successor cannot finish until the predecessor has finished.

questions.question: An old IT support system must continue operating until the replacement support system has started functioning. Which dependency best represents this situation?
questions.explanation: Start-to-Finish means the successor cannot finish until the predecessor has started; it is a rare dependency type.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Estimating Activity Durations?
questions.option_a: A. To determine how long individual project activities are expected to take
questions.option_d: D. To define team authority levels
questions.explanation: Estimating Activity Durations predicts the time required to complete individual activities using available information and resources.

questions.question: A project manager uses historical data from a similar previous mobile application to estimate the duration of UI development. Which technique is being used?
questions.explanation: Analogous Estimating uses historical information from similar past projects and is particularly useful during early project stages.

questions.question: A developer is expected to produce 100 lines of code per day, and a module is estimated to require 1,000 lines. Which estimation technique is illustrated?
questions.explanation: Parametric Estimating uses measurable variables and statistical relationships. Here, 1,000 lines divided by 100 lines per day gives 10 days.

questions.question: For an activity, the optimistic estimate is 4 days, the most likely estimate is 7 days, and the pessimistic estimate is 16 days. Using the lecture's three-point formula, what is the expected duration?
questions.explanation: Using E = (O + 4M + P) / 6, E = (4 + 4(7) + 16) / 6 = 48/6 = 8 days. Therefore the correct option should be C.

questions.question: Which estimation technique separately estimates individual activities and combines them to determine the total duration or cost?
questions.explanation: Bottom-Up Estimating estimates individual activities separately and combines the estimates. It is highly accurate but time-consuming.

questions.question: A project manager has limited information and needs a quick duration estimate based on a previous project that is closely similar. Which technique is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Analogous Estimating is quick and useful in early project stages, particularly when a closely similar historical project exists.

questions.question: Which process combines activity sequences, durations, resource requirements, and scheduling constraints to create the project schedule model?
questions.explanation: Develop Schedule analyzes activity sequences, durations, resources, and constraints to establish the project schedule.

questions.question: What does float or slack represent in Critical Path Method?
questions.option_a: A. The total cost of an activity
questions.option_b: B. The time an activity can be delayed without affecting the project
questions.option_c: C. The number of resources assigned to an activity
questions.option_d: D. The time required to negotiate a contract
questions.explanation: Float or slack is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the project.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the major steps of CPM described in the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. List activities, define dependencies, estimate durations, create network diagram, calculate ES/EF/LS/LF, identify critical path
questions.option_b: B. Select vendor, negotiate contract, calculate CPI, archive records, identify critical path
questions.option_c: C. Estimate cost, acquire resources, close procurement, calculate SPI, create WBS
questions.option_d: D. Define milestones, conduct procurement audit, calculate AC, assign vendors, estimate resources
questions.explanation: The lecture lists these six steps as the CPM procedure.

questions.question: A project contains two independent paths. Path 1 takes 18 days and Path 2 takes 25 days. Based only on this information, which path determines the minimum project completion time?
questions.explanation: The longest dependent sequence determines the minimum possible project duration, so the 25-day path is critical based on the information provided.

questions.question: Which process focuses on monitoring project schedule performance, managing schedule changes, and taking corrective actions?
questions.explanation: Controlling the Schedule compares actual progress with the plan, manages changes, and applies corrective actions.

questions.question: A project manager discovers that actual progress is significantly behind the planned schedule and reallocates resources to reduce the delay. Which activity is being performed?
questions.explanation: Applying corrective actions can involve adjusting resources, timelines, or activities to reduce schedule delays.

questions.question: What does Planned Value (PV) represent in Earned Value Management?
questions.option_a: A. Actual cost spent on completed work
questions.option_b: B. Budgeted value of planned work
questions.explanation: PV is the budgeted value of work that was planned.

questions.question: What does Earned Value (EV) represent?
questions.option_a: A. The value of completed work
questions.option_b: B. The budgeted value of planned work
questions.option_c: C. The actual cost spent on completed work
questions.explanation: EV represents the value of work that has actually been completed.

questions.question: A project has EV = $75,000 and PV = $100,000. What is the Schedule Variance (SV)?
questions.explanation: SV = EV - PV = $75,000 - $100,000 = -$25,000. A negative SV indicates the project is behind schedule.

questions.question: A project has EV = $120,000 and PV = $100,000. What does the Schedule Variance indicate?
questions.option_a: A. The project is behind schedule
questions.option_b: B. The project is ahead of schedule
questions.option_c: C. The project is over budget
questions.option_d: D. The project is exactly on schedule
questions.explanation: SV = EV - PV = $20,000, which is positive. According to the lecture, SV > 0 indicates the project is ahead of schedule.

questions.question: A project has EV = $80,000 and PV = $100,000. What is the Schedule Performance Index (SPI)?
questions.explanation: SPI = EV/PV = 80,000/100,000 = 0.80. An SPI below 1 indicates the project is behind schedule.

questions.question: A project has EV = $150,000 and PV = $150,000. What does its SPI indicate?
questions.option_b: B. It is ahead of schedule
questions.option_d: D. It is necessarily under budget
questions.explanation: SPI = EV/PV = 1. An SPI of 1 indicates the project is on schedule.

questions.question: A project has EV = $90,000 and AC = $110,000. What is the Cost Variance (CV)?
questions.explanation: CV = EV - AC = $90,000 - $110,000 = -$20,000. A negative CV indicates the project is over budget.

questions.question: A project has EV = $90,000 and AC = $110,000. What does its CPI indicate?
questions.option_a: A. It is cost efficient because CPI is greater than 1
questions.option_b: B. It is experiencing a cost overrun because CPI is less than 1
questions.option_c: C. It is ahead of schedule because CPI is less than 1
questions.option_d: D. It is exactly on budget because CPI equals 1
questions.explanation: CPI = EV/AC = 90,000/110,000 ≈ 0.82. A CPI below 1 indicates a cost overrun.

questions.question: A project has EV = $120,000, PV = $100,000, and AC = $100,000. Which interpretation is correct?
questions.option_a: A. Behind schedule and over budget
questions.option_b: B. Ahead of schedule and exactly on budget
questions.option_c: C. On schedule and over budget
questions.option_d: D. Behind schedule and under budget
questions.explanation: SV = $20,000, so the project is ahead of schedule. CV = $20,000, so it is under budget. CPI = 1.2 and SPI = 1.2.

questions.question: A project reports SPI = 0.75 and CPI = 1.15. What is the best interpretation?
questions.option_a: A. The project is ahead of schedule and over budget
questions.option_b: B. The project is behind schedule but cost efficient
questions.option_c: C. The project is on schedule and over budget
questions.option_d: D. The project is ahead of schedule and exactly on budget
questions.explanation: SPI below 1 indicates the project is behind schedule, while CPI above 1 indicates cost efficiency.

questions.question: A software project is behind schedule but under budget. Which EVM result combination is consistent with this situation?
questions.explanation: SPI < 1 indicates the project is behind schedule, while CPI > 1 indicates it is cost efficient.

questions.question: A project manager observes that a supplier is meeting the required cost but repeatedly failing quality requirements. What is the most appropriate immediate procurement focus?
questions.option_a: A. Monitor seller performance and review deliverables
questions.explanation: Controlling Procurements includes monitoring seller performance and validating that deliverables meet project specifications.

questions.question: A project manager knows that a future project phase has uncertain requirements but the next two weeks of work are well understood. Which scheduling approach best matches the lecture?
questions.explanation: Rolling Wave Planning provides detailed planning for near-term work while future work remains at a higher level until more information becomes available.

questions.question: A project manager first estimates every small development activity separately and then combines those estimates to determine the overall development effort. What is the strongest reason this approach may be selected?
questions.option_a: A. It is highly accurate, although time-consuming
questions.option_b: B. It requires no knowledge of individual activities
questions.option_c: C. It only works when historical projects are identical
questions.option_d: D. It eliminates the need to consider resources
questions.explanation: Bottom-Up Estimating provides detailed estimates and is described as highly accurate, but it requires more time.

questions.question: A project team has a vendor contract, but a required deliverable is discovered to be inconsistent with the agreed specifications. Which action most directly addresses the problem during procurement control?
questions.option_a: A. Review the deliverable against project specifications
questions.explanation: Reviewing deliverables is a controlling procurement activity used to validate that procured products or services meet project specifications.

questions.question: A project manager discovers that planned resource allocation differs substantially from actual resource usage. Which combination of actions is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: A. Compare actual versus planned usage and optimize resource allocation
questions.option_b: B. Issue an RFP and negotiate with vendors
questions.option_c: C. Calculate only the project's SPI
questions.option_d: D. Close all procurement contracts immediately
questions.explanation: Controlling Resources explicitly includes comparing actual versus planned usage and optimizing resource allocation.

questions.question: A project has three paths with durations of 12, 19, and 15 days. Assuming each is a dependent path from project start to finish, which path is critical?
questions.option_d: D. All paths are automatically critical
questions.explanation: The critical path is the longest sequence of dependent activities. Based on the given durations, the 19-day path determines the minimum project duration.

questions.question: A project has PV = $200,000, EV = $160,000, and AC = $180,000. Which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: A. The project is ahead of schedule and under budget
questions.option_b: B. The project is behind schedule and over budget
questions.option_c: C. The project is on schedule and over budget
questions.option_d: D. The project is ahead of schedule and over budget
questions.explanation: SV = 160,000 - 200,000 = -40,000 and CV = 160,000 - 180,000 = -20,000. Both negative values indicate the project is behind schedule and over budget.

questions.question: For the same project with PV = $200,000, EV = $160,000, and AC = $180,000, which pair of performance indices is correct?

A project manager must choose between two suppliers. Supplier X has the lowest price but poor technical capability and a weak delivery record. Supplier Y costs more but has strong quality, experience, technical capability, and delivery performance. Based on the lecture's procurement approach, what should the manager do?
questions.option_a: A. Automatically select Supplier X because price is the only relevant factor
questions.option_b: B. Evaluate both suppliers using multiple selection criteria
questions.option_c: C. Select Supplier Y without evaluating any criteria
questions.option_d: D. Ignore delivery performance because it is unrelated to procurement
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies cost, quality, experience, technical capability, and delivery schedules as proposal evaluation factors, so selection should use multiple criteria.

questions.question: A project manager is deciding whether to hire an external specialist, but first needs to determine whether the required expertise already exists internally. Which combination of concepts is most directly relevant?
questions.option_a: A. Make-or-buy analysis and resource planning
questions.option_d: D. Finish-to-finish dependencies and procurement audits
questions.explanation: Make-or-buy analysis addresses internal versus external acquisition, while resource planning identifies required internal resources and capabilities.

questions.question: A team has the required number of developers, but their collaboration is poor and conflicts are reducing performance. Which response best matches the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Acquire additional physical resources only
questions.option_b: B. Use team development and team management activities such as communication improvement, conflict resolution, and feedback
questions.option_c: C. Replace the schedule with a Gantt chart
questions.explanation: Developing the Team improves collaboration and communication, while Managing the Team addresses performance, feedback, motivation, and conflict resolution.

questions.question: A project manager wants to understand whether schedule performance is improving and whether corrective action is required. Which combination of Schedule Management activities is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: A. Track progress, analyze schedule variance, and apply corrective actions
questions.option_b: B. Issue RFQs, negotiate contracts, and archive procurement records
questions.option_c: C. Conduct team-building activities and assign team members
questions.explanation: Controlling the Schedule involves tracking actual progress, analyzing variances, managing changes, and applying corrective actions.
